Map pick by Firing Squad.

Demos: [https://www.quakeworld.nu/w/images/f/fb/Infinity_-fs-_vs_gb_dm3.qwz infinity (FS)]

"This match began with FS taking both quad and pent but managing to kill their own guy at Quad. FS takes YA while GB take to the RA for cover. 19 minutes, FS up by 6 frags. FS begin to run the armors, sending in a juiced up player after the RA at regular intervals while keeping a strong check on the YA. GB amass at quad but FS appears and drive them of, taking the powerup with some good coordination. FS uses the quad to clean the rl-box and bridge. 16 minutes left and FS have taken to the lead by 37 frags. Atomalf from GB manages to steal the YA and then kill the quad. GB make somewhat of a comeback by taking both the pent and the quad. The quad is quickly put down, but the pent does some damage and helps GB hold on to RA. 14 mins left, FS up by 31. GB launces a counteroffensive, attacking YA and getting the next quad. There's a lot of small skirmishes, FS still manages to come out on top. With 11 minutes left, they lead by 36 frags and have good control over YA and quad. Amazingly, GB again manages to take both pent and quad. They keep one man at quad and the rest gather strenght at RA. FS keeps running the armors, not letting GB rest up at RA for very long. 8 minutes left sees FS in the lead by 62 frags. FS takes the quad and owns the rl-area. GB scrambling for positions. With 6 minutes to go, FS is up by 80 and keeping the level pretty much under control, getting the next few quads. At the 5-minute mark, FS takes the pent and kills GB's quadguy. 4 mins left, FS up by 101. FS takes the next couple of quads, pretty much running the show now. GB manages to discharge one of the FS-quads, but otherwise, FS are clearly in control. 1 minute left, FS up by 124 ... mixed frags the last seconds ... GG FS!" -Ego === DM2 === FS: 178 - GB: 122
[[Image:Fs gb dm2.gif]]
Map pick by Giant Balls.

"First quad goes to GB but FS soon take high-rl and the middle room, pushing GB into lowe rl. FS control tele and are racking up frags quickly. 19 minutes left, FS up by 9 frags. GB holding the backroom. FS takes the quad and attacks low, they increase their lead to 23 in the next minute and are looking very strong. They take the next quad and are now clearly in control of the tele, high-rl and middle-room. GB still keeping low-rl though. 16 minutes left, FS in the lead by 39 frags. FS makes a great two-pronged attack against low-rl, jumping in from both passages to take down some tough GB-resistance. Again, they take quad and apparently have boxed in GB in lower and backroom. GB seem to realise that they are getting creamed in the low-rl and abandon it for the bigroom instead. 12 minutes left, FS by 72 frags. GB attacks the middle-room with rocketlaunchers. FS still holds tele and gets the next quad. 8 minutes, FS up by 93 frags. GB are biting back and attack FS positions from the bigroom. FS holds most of the level, but GB still manages to swipe the quad! With the quads and their RL's, GB take tele and middle-room. As Little Horn from FS begins to lag suddenly (playing from a university line), GB also clear the low-rl and suddenly look very strong. FS all retreat to backroom, apparently confused about the turnaround. They seem content at waiting out the last five minutes of the game, but this is not a working strategy as they soon discover. With five minutes left, FS have lost some from their initial lead, and now have +73 frags. They have lost most of the level and are mostly just wandering about. GB seize their chance and start racking up the frags. With three minutes left, FS still lead by 58 frags and make a comeback by taking quad. GB are still fighting stronger and the last minute, they take a quad and do some more damage ... still, FS have again proven their skill, taking this level with +56 frags. GG to both teams, nice comeback from GB, but perhaps a bit to non-aggressive approach when FS lost positions." -Ego == Summary == * Score: 2-0 * Total frags ** FS: 371 ** GB: 182 __NOTOC__ [[Category:Matchreports]]
